title: The Sudden change in the weather
subtitle: 天气气候 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）
meta: 主题语境：天气气候（人与自然·自然生态·天气与气候）　|　核心词汇：sudden　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sudden 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1981 the director wrote of ① a sudden change in the weather in the poster, and everybody in the theatre said at once that it was ② so sudden that nobody in the theatre would go near it. Three nights on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the director, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the sudden ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the sudden change in the weather that anybody there had ever seen, or so the poster for August 1975 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too sudden to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the actor who had come to help; the sudden ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the script at the far stage, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a sudden end of the talk, and said that no actor in his right mind would call it ⑥ as sudden as the end of the talk they had once had in the old theatre. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was sudden or not, and he said so.

By 1988 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the poster. What the line asked for was ⑦ something sudden, and nothing besides. The actor from the next theatre called the whole plan ⑧ quite sudden; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the poster kept the names of the sudden ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1991, in the rain, she wrote of another sudden change in the weather in the same poster, and the work, which took two nights, seemed ⑨ no less sudden than anybody had expected. ⑩ The sudden end of the talk that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1993, was the one she could never quite name; the sudden ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 突然（前置定语 a sudden change in the weather：1981 年导演在戏报里记下的那件突然的突变）
B. adj. 突然／意外（两处加强说法：so sudden that … 与 no less sudden than …）
C. adj. 突然／意外（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 突然（表语 too sudden to do：母亲觉得它太突然，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 意外（前置定语 a sudden end of the talk：叔叔把整件事称作一桩意外的戛然而止）
F. adj. 意外（同级比较 as sudden as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩谈话的戛然而止相比）
G. adj. 意外（后置定语 something sudden：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 意外（受程度副词修饰 quite sudden：那位演员的评价）

items.q: a sudden change in the weather
the sudden change in the weather that
a sudden end of the talk
The sudden end of the talk that

answers.why: sudden 意为“突然”，1981 年导演在戏报里记下的是“一件突然的突变”，此处作前置定语 a sudden change in the weather。
sudden 意为“突然”，此处用 so sudden that 结构，说它突然到戏院里没人敢靠近。
sudden 意为“突然”，戏报上 八月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的突然天气的突变，等于最高级的说法。
sudden 意为“突然”，母亲认为这件东西“太突然了，谁也用不上”，too sudden to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
sudden 意为“意外”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩意外的戛然而止”，此处作前置定语 a sudden end of the talk。
sudden 意为“意外”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩谈话的戛然而止一样意外”，同级比较用 as sudden as。
sudden 意为“意外”，戏报上那半行字要的是“意外的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something sudden。
sudden 意为“意外”，邻戏院来的那位演员认为这套计划“相当意外”，quite 修饰原级 sudden。
sudden 意为“意外”，no less sudden than 表示“其意外不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之意外不亚于任何人的预料。
sudden 意为“意外”，母亲 1993 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的意外戛然而止”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1981 年，导演在戏报里记下了一件突然的突变。（a sudden change in the weather）
它突然到戏院里没有一个人敢靠近。（so sudden that …）
母亲觉得它太突然，谁也用不上。（too sudden to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩意外的戛然而止。（a sudden end of the talk）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩谈话的戛然而止一样意外。（as sudden as …）
到了 1988 年，戏报上只剩半行字：要的是一件意外的东西。（something sudden）
answers: In 1981 the director wrote of a sudden change in the weather in the poster.
It was so sudden that nobody in the theatre would go near it.
My mother thought it too sudden to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a sudden end of the talk.
He said nobody would call it as sudden as the end of the talk they had once had.
By 1988 the poster asked for nothing but something sudden.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sudden 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1981 the director wrote of a sudden change in the weather in the poster, and nobody forgot it.
It was the sudden change in the weather that anybody there had ever seen, or so the poster says.
My mother thought it too sudden to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a sudden end of the talk, and nobody argued with him.
The actor from the next theatre called the plan quite sudden, and everybody laughed.
The sudden ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
